quotes.text: But custom doesn't always mean better. A per tenant extension gives you a close fit, but someone has to own it. That means keeping notes, testing changes, and arranging support when your company changes the process

quotes.text: A manager can approve an app on paper, but the person who enters orders may spot a missing field or an extra step within minutes.

quotes.text: If a vendor can't explain what its app does with your information, don't put that app into a process that handles customer records or financial data.

chapters.title: How extensions change your daily work

takeaways: Business Central extensions add fields, pages, reports, permissions and integrations in their own package, so the standard application stays intact and updates cause less repair work.
Use Microsoft or ISV apps from AppSource for common needs and per-tenant extensions only for processes unique to your company, with a clear owner for support and testing.
Before installing, check publisher, supported versions, pricing, documentation, data flows and permissions, test real cases in a sandbox, and keep a record of every installed extension.
hook: Business Central covers most core processes, but every company has gaps such as special shipping, local reports or bank integrations. This Simply Explained episode is for Business Central users, finance teams and admins who decide which add-ons to install. It explains the types of extensions and what to check on security, data and support before an app becomes part of daily work.
